potential-koto-ga-dekiru.detail: Turns the action before こと into an ability or possibility: "can do..."

examples.japanese: 日本語を話すことができます。
examples.english: I can speak Japanese.
examples.note: Verb + ことができる marks ability.

potential-dekiru.detail: Uses できる to show that an action is possible, often after a する noun.

examples.japanese: 一人で勉強できます。
examples.english: I can study by myself.
examples.note: Noun + できる often marks the potential form of a する verb.

obligation-nakereba-naranai.detail: Says an action is necessary or required. Casual forms like なきゃ and なくちゃ carry the same basic idea.

examples.japanese: 明日までに払わなければならない。
examples.english: I have to pay by tomorrow.
examples.note: The first clause is required.

permission-not-required-nakutemo-ii.detail: Says the action is not required, or that not doing it is okay.

examples.japanese: 今日は来なくてもいいです。
examples.english: You do not have to come today.
examples.note: Negative て-form + もいい removes obligation.

prohibition-tewa-ikenai.detail: Marks an action as not allowed or unacceptable. Casual ちゃだめ and じゃだめ are included.

examples.japanese: ここで写真を撮ってはいけません。
examples.english: You must not take photos here.
examples.note: てはいけない is a direct prohibition.

permission-temo-ii.detail: Means it is okay to do the action before てもいい. Negative variants can ask or say whether it is not okay.

examples.japanese: 水を飲んでもいいです。
examples.english: It is okay to drink water.
examples.note: て-form + もいい grants permission.

request-te-kudasai.detail: Makes a direct but polite request. くださいませんか is softer.

examples.japanese: ゆっくり話してください。
examples.english: Please speak slowly.
examples.note: て-form + ください requests an action.

polite-request-te-itadakemasen-ka.detail: A softer request that asks someone to do something for you politely.

examples.japanese: もう一度説明していただけませんか。
examples.english: Could you please explain it one more time?
examples.note: ていただけませんか is a polite request form.

request-naide-kudasai.detail: Politely asks someone not to do an action.

examples.japanese: ここで走らないでください。
examples.english: Please do not run here.
examples.note: ないでください is the negative request form.

advice-hou-ga-ii.detail: Gives advice or says one option is better.

examples.japanese: 早く寝たほうがいいです。
examples.english: It is better to go to bed early.
examples.note: Often follows past tense for advice.

command-nasai.detail: A command form often used by adults toward children or in instructions.

examples.japanese: 宿題をしなさい。
examples.english: Do your homework.
examples.note: Stem + なさい gives an instruction.

experience-ta-koto-ga-aru.detail: Uses a past verb plus ことがある to talk about having had an experience.

examples.japanese: 京都に行ったことがあります。
examples.english: I have been to Kyoto.
examples.note: Past verb + ことがある marks experience.

completion-te-shimau.detail: Can show that an action is completed, often with a feeling of regret, surprise, or accident.

examples.japanese: 財布を忘れてしまいました。
examples.english: I unfortunately forgot my wallet.
examples.note: てしまう can add regret or completion.

attempt-te-miru.detail: Means to try an action and see what happens.

examples.japanese: 新しい店で食べてみます。
examples.english: I will try eating at the new shop.
examples.note: て-form + みる is experimental trying.

preparation-te-oku.short: do in advance or leave as is
preparation-te-oku.detail: Often marks an action done ahead of time, or a state intentionally left alone. Casual とく and どく are included.

examples.japanese: 旅行の前に予約しておきます。
examples.english: I will make a reservation before the trip.
examples.note: ておく prepares for later.

desire-other-te-hoshii.detail: Says the speaker wants someone else to do the action.

examples.japanese: もう少し待ってほしいです。
examples.english: I want you to wait a little longer.
examples.note: てほしい points desire at someone else's action.

benefactive-te-kureru-morau.detail: Combines て-form with giving or receiving verbs to show who benefits from an action.

examples.japanese: 先生が説明してくださいました。
examples.english: The teacher kindly explained it.
examples.note: The helper verb shows benefit and direction.

change-you-ni-naru.short: come to do or become so that
change-you-ni-naru.detail: Shows a new ability, habit, or state developing over time.

examples.japanese: 漢字が読めるようになりました。
examples.english: I became able to read kanji.
examples.note: Often describes gradual change.

habit-you-ni-suru.detail: Shows an intentional effort to make an action happen regularly or reliably.

examples.japanese: 毎日復習するようにしています。
examples.english: I try to review every day.
examples.note: ようにする describes deliberate effort.

verb-suru.detail: Flags する as a core irregular verb and as the helper that turns many nouns into actions.

examples.japanese: 質問する答えを探す。
examples.english: Find answers to questions.
examples.note: する can attach to a noun to create an action verb.

choice-ni-suru.detail: Marks a choice or an intentional change into the state before にする.

examples.japanese: 飲み物はお茶にします。
examples.english: I will have tea.
examples.note: Noun + にする is used for choosing or making something a certain way.

change-ku-suru.detail: Uses an i-adjective adverbial form plus する to make something become that quality.

examples.japanese: 部屋を明るくしました。
examples.english: I made the room brighter.
examples.note: い-adjective stem + くする marks intentional change.

change-ku-naru-ni-naru.detail: Shows that something becomes a new quality or state.

examples.japanese: 日本語が少し上手になりました。
examples.english: My Japanese got a little better.
examples.note: Noun/な-adjective + になる and い-adjective + くなる mark change.

copula-desu-da.detail: Links a noun or adjective to a statement in plain or polite style.

examples.japanese: 今日は休みです。
examples.english: Today is a day off.
examples.note: です is the polite copula.

negative-copula-dewa-nai.detail: Negates a noun or な-adjective statement.

examples.japanese: これは私の本じゃない。
examples.english: This is not my book.
examples.note: じゃない is the casual contraction of ではない.

formal-copula-de-aru.detail: A formal written-style copula often used in essays, explanations, and news.

examples.japanese: これは重要な問題である。
examples.english: This is an important problem.
examples.note: である is a formal version of だ/です.

voice-causative-passive.detail: Combines causative and passive meaning: someone is made to do an action, often unwillingly.

examples.japanese: 子どものころ、野菜を食べさせられました。
examples.english: When I was a child, I was made to eat vegetables.
examples.note: Regex can only flag the form; context decides the exact verb.

voice-causative.detail: Adds a causer: someone makes, lets, or has someone else do the action.

examples.japanese: 母は子どもを遊ばせた。
examples.english: The mother let the child play.
examples.note: Causative can mean make or let.

voice-passive-potential.detail: This ending can mark passive voice, ability, or respectful speech; context decides which reading fits.

examples.japanese: この漢字はよく見られます。
examples.english: This kanji is often seen.
examples.note: Surface regex cannot fully disambiguate passive, potential, and honorific.

evidence-rashii-mitai.detail: Expresses appearance, hearsay, tendency, or resemblance depending on the form and context.

examples.japanese: 明日は雨らしいです。
examples.english: Apparently it will rain tomorrow.
examples.note: らしい often reports what one has heard.

modality-kamoshirenai.detail: Softens a statement into a possibility rather than a firm claim.

examples.japanese: 彼は来ないかもしれません。
examples.english: He might not come.
examples.note: かも is a casual short form.

modality-deshou-darou.detail: Adds probability, expectation, or a confirmation-seeking tone.

examples.japanese: 明日は晴れるでしょう。
examples.english: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.
examples.note: でしょう is polite; だろう is plainer.

quotation-to-omou.detail: Marks the content of a thought or statement before 思う.

examples.japanese: これは便利だと思います。
examples.english: I think this is convenient.
examples.note: The phrase before と is the thought content.

attempt-you-to-suru.short: try to or be about to
attempt-you-to-suru.detail: Uses the volitional form plus とする for an attempted action or something about to happen.

examples.japanese: 出かけようとした時、電話が鳴った。
examples.english: Just as I was about to go out, the phone rang.
examples.note: Volitional + とする marks trying or being about to act.

plan-tsumori-yotei.detail: つもり points to intention, while 予定 points to a plan or schedule.

examples.japanese: 来年日本へ行くつもりです。
examples.english: I intend to go to Japan next year.
examples.note: つもり is intention; 予定 is a plan.

expectation-hazu.detail: Marks a strong expectation based on what the speaker knows.

examples.japanese: 彼はもう着いたはずです。
examples.english: He should have arrived already.
examples.note: はず signals a reasoned expectation.

reasoning-wake.detail: Points to a logical reason or conclusion, with negative forms often meaning not necessarily or cannot reasonably.

examples.japanese: 高いわけではありません。
examples.english: It is not necessarily expensive.
examples.note: Specific わけ forms may be more precise if also detected.

reasoning-wake-dewa-nai.detail: Says a statement is not fully or necessarily true.

examples.japanese: 嫌いなわけではない。
examples.english: It is not that I dislike it.
examples.note: Often softens or qualifies a previous implication.

examples.japanese: 彼が知らないわけがない。
examples.english: There is no way he does not know.
examples.note: わけがない rejects the possibility.

constraint-wake-ni-wa-ikanai.detail: Says one cannot do something because of duty, social pressure, or circumstances.

examples.japanese: 約束を破るわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I cannot break the promise.
examples.note: The barrier is often social or practical.

purpose-tame-ni.short: for the sake of or in order to
purpose-tame-ni.detail: Links an action or noun to a purpose, goal, or beneficiary.

examples.japanese: 家族のために働いています。
examples.english: I work for my family.
examples.note: ために marks purpose or benefit.

purpose-you-ni.short: so that or in the way that
purpose-you-ni.detail: Can mark a goal, desired result, or manner of doing something.

examples.japanese: 忘れないようにメモします。
examples.english: I will write a note so I do not forget.
examples.note: This is broader than ようになる and ようにする.

timing-tokoro.detail: Frames an action as about to happen, happening now, just happened, or as a situation.

examples.japanese: 今、出かけるところです。
examples.english: I am just about to go out.
examples.note: ところ focuses on the moment or situation.

simultaneous-nagara.detail: Connects two actions done at the same time by the same subject.

examples.japanese: 音楽を聞きながら勉強します。
examples.english: I study while listening to music.
examples.note: ながら joins simultaneous actions.

state-mama.detail: Keeps a state unchanged while another action or situation continues.

examples.japanese: 電気をつけたまま寝てしまった。
examples.english: I fell asleep with the light still on.
examples.note: まま preserves the previous state.

list-tari.detail: Lists example actions without claiming the list is complete.

examples.japanese: 週末は映画を見たり本を読んだりします。
examples.english: On weekends I do things like watch movies and read books.
examples.note: たり usually appears in pairs but can be single.

limitation-bakari.short: only, just did, or nothing but
limitation-bakari.detail: Can mark a recent completed action or a sense of only or nothing but depending on context.

examples.japanese: 彼はゲームばかりしています。
examples.english: He does nothing but play games.
examples.note: ばかり can also mean just did after past tense.

recent-ta-bakari.detail: Uses a past form plus ばかり to say something has just happened recently from the speaker's point of view.

examples.japanese: 日本に来たばかりです。
examples.english: I just came to Japan.
examples.note: Past form + ばかり focuses on recent completion.

limitation-dake-shika.detail: だけ means only; しか usually pairs with a negative ending to mean nothing but.

examples.japanese: 百円しかありません。
examples.english: I have only 100 yen.
examples.note: しか expects a negative predicate.

degree-hodo-kurai.detail: Marks approximate amount or the degree to which something is true.

examples.japanese: 一時間ぐらい待ちました。
examples.english: I waited about an hour.
examples.note: ほど often emphasizes degree; くらい can be approximate.

role-toshite.short: as or in the role of
role-toshite.detail: Marks the role, capacity, or standpoint from which something is true.

examples.japanese: 医者として働いています。
examples.english: I work as a doctor.
examples.note: として marks role or capacity.

relation-ni-yotte.short: by, depending on, or because of
relation-ni-yotte.detail: Can mark means, agent in passive sentences, cause, or variation depending on context.

examples.japanese: 国によって習慣が違います。
examples.english: Customs differ depending on the country.
examples.note: によって is highly context-dependent.

topic-ni-tsuite.detail: Marks the topic being discussed, considered, or investigated.

examples.japanese: 日本の歴史について調べています。
examples.english: I am researching Japanese history.
examples.note: について is a topic marker.

target-ni-taishite.short: toward, against, or in contrast to
target-ni-taishite.detail: Marks the target of an attitude or action, or sets up a contrast.

examples.japanese: 子どもに対して優しい。
examples.english: She is kind toward children.
examples.note: に対して points at the target.

concession-ni-mo-kakawarazu.detail: Connects two facts when the second happens despite the first.

examples.japanese: 雨にもかかわらず試合は行われた。
examples.english: The game was held despite the rain.
examples.note: Formal concessive connector.

concession-kuse-ni.detail: Marks a contradiction with a blaming or critical tone.

examples.japanese: 知らないくせに文句を言う。
examples.english: He complains even though he does not know.
examples.note: くせに often sounds critical.

suffix-tachi.short: marks a group or plural set
suffix-tachi.detail: Attaches to a person, pronoun, or animate noun to point to that person and their group, or to a plural group.

examples.japanese: 私たちは学生です。
examples.english: We are students.
examples.note: Often used for people or animate groups.

particle-wa.detail: Read it as as for and look to the rest of the sentence for the new information.

examples.japanese: 私は学生です。
examples.english: I am a student.
examples.note: は marks the topic, not always the grammatical subject.

particle-ga.detail: Highlights the subject of the clause, often when that subject is new or important.

examples.japanese: 猫が走ります。
examples.english: The cat runs.
examples.note: が often introduces or focuses a subject.

particle-wo.detail: The phrase before を is usually what the following verb acts on.

examples.japanese: 水を飲みます。
examples.english: I drink water.
examples.note: を marks the direct object.

particle-de.short: marks where or how an action happens
particle-de.detail: Often points to the setting, tool, method, or conditions for the action.

examples.japanese: 駅で待ちます。
examples.english: I will wait at the station.
examples.note: で marks place, means, cause, or context.

particle-ni.short: marks a target, point, time, or adverbial role
particle-ni.detail: Think of に as pinning the action to a destination, time, target, or manner.

examples.japanese: 駅に行きます。
examples.english: I go to the station.
examples.note: に anchors time, target, or direction.

particle-e.detail: Marks the direction or destination of movement.

examples.japanese: 学校へ行きます。
examples.english: I go to school.
examples.note: へ emphasizes direction more than arrival.

particle-to.short: marks with, and, or quoted content
particle-to.detail: Can mark who someone does something with, exact quoted content, comparison, or a complete list.

examples.japanese: 友だちと話します。
examples.english: I talk with my friend.
examples.note: と has several basic particle uses.

particle-no.detail: The phrase before の modifies or belongs with the noun that follows.

examples.japanese: 私の本です。
examples.english: It is my book.
examples.note: の links nouns or nominalizes phrases.

particle-mo.detail: Adds the marked item to a set, or emphasizes extent with quantities.

examples.japanese: 私も行きます。
examples.english: I will go too.
examples.note: も adds another item to the conversation.

particle-ya.detail: Lists examples without implying the list is complete.

examples.japanese: パンや卵を買いました。
examples.english: I bought bread, eggs, and things like that.
examples.note: や creates a non-exhaustive list.

aspect-te-iru.detail: Shows an action in progress, or a state that remains after something changed.

examples.japanese: 今、本を読んでいます。
examples.english: I am reading a book now.
examples.note: ている can be progressive or resultative.

aspect-te-aru.detail: Shows a result intentionally left in place after an action.

examples.japanese: 窓が開けてあります。
examples.english: The window has been opened and left that way.
examples.note: てある suggests an intentional prepared state.

aspect-te-kuru.short: come to do or develop toward now
aspect-te-kuru.detail: Shows movement toward the speaker or a change developing up to now.

examples.japanese: 雨が降ってきました。
examples.english: It has started raining.
examples.note: てくる can be physical or temporal.

aspect-te-iku.short: go on doing or develop away
aspect-te-iku.detail: Shows movement away from the speaker or a change continuing into the future.

examples.japanese: これからも勉強していきます。
examples.english: I will keep studying from now on.
examples.note: ていく often looks forward or outward.

desire-tai.detail: Attaches to a verb stem to say the speaker wants to do that action.

examples.japanese: 日本へ行きたいです。
examples.english: I want to go to Japan.
examples.note: たい describes the speaker's desire.

ease-yasui-nikui.detail: Shows that an action is easy, difficult, or psychologically hard to do.

examples.japanese: この本は読みやすいです。
examples.english: This book is easy to read.
examples.note: Stem + やすい or にくい describes ease.

excess-sugiru.detail: Shows that something goes beyond a suitable amount or degree.

examples.japanese: 食べすぎました。
examples.english: I ate too much.
examples.note: Stem/adjective + すぎる marks excess.

method-kata.detail: Attaches to a verb stem to mean the way to do that action.

examples.japanese: 使い方を教えてください。
examples.english: Please teach me how to use it.
examples.note: Stem + 方 creates a method noun.

negative-nai.detail: Turns the verb or expression into do not, is not, or did not.

examples.japanese: 今日は行きません。
examples.english: I will not go today.
examples.note: ない and ません are negative endings.

polite-past-mashita.detail: A polite ます-form verb in the past tense: did or was/were.

examples.japanese: 昨日、勉強しました。
examples.english: I studied yesterday.
examples.note: ました is polite past.

polite-masu.detail: Softens the verb into polite speech; tense depends on the surrounding sentence.

examples.japanese: 毎日勉強します。
examples.english: I study every day.
examples.note: ます is polite non-past.

conditional-tara.detail: Turns the first clause into the condition or timing for what follows: if, when, or after.

examples.japanese: 雨が降ったら、行きません。
examples.english: If it rains, I will not go.
examples.note: たら can mean if, when, or after.

conditional-ba.detail: Marks the condition that needs to be true for the next clause to happen.

examples.japanese: 安ければ買います。
examples.english: If it is cheap, I will buy it.
examples.note: ば creates a conditional clause.

conditional-ba-ii.short: should do or should have done
conditional-ba-ii.detail: Can give advice, ask what to do, or express regret about what should have happened.

examples.japanese: もっと早く聞けばよかった。
examples.english: I should have asked earlier.
examples.note: ばよかった often expresses regret.

conditional-nara.short: if it is the case that
conditional-nara.detail: Sets up a condition, topic, or assumption before giving advice or a result.

examples.japanese: 日本へ行くなら、春がいいです。
examples.english: If you are going to Japan, spring is good.
examples.note: なら often responds to or narrows a topic.

conditional-to.detail: Marks a natural, automatic, or expected result that follows from the first clause.

examples.japanese: このボタンを押すと、音が出ます。
examples.english: When you press this button, a sound plays.
examples.note: と conditionals often describe predictable results.

concession-temo-demo.detail: Adds a condition that does not change the result.

examples.japanese: 雨が降っても行きます。
examples.english: I will go even if it rains.
examples.note: て-form + も creates even if.

reason-node.detail: Gives the reason or cause for the following statement, usually with a softer tone than から.

examples.japanese: 電車が遅れたので、遅刻しました。
examples.english: The train was late, so I was late.
examples.note: ので is often softer than から.

reason-kara.detail: Can mean because, from, or after, depending on what surrounds it.

examples.japanese: 寒いから、上着を着ます。
examples.english: It is cold, so I will wear a jacket.
examples.note: から is broad and context-dependent.

appearance-sou.detail: Describes how something seems from appearance, or that an action looks likely to happen.

examples.japanese: このケーキはおいしそうです。
examples.english: This cake looks delicious.
examples.note: そう describes appearance when attached to a stem.

hearsay-sou-da.detail: Reports information heard from another source.

examples.japanese: ニュースによると、雪が降るそうです。
examples.english: According to the news, it will snow.
examples.note: Plain-form clause + そうだ reports hearsay.

volitional-you.detail: Often expresses let us, I will, or a suggestion to do something together.

examples.japanese: 一緒に帰ろう。
examples.english: Let us go home together.
examples.note: Volitional forms can be proposals or intentions.

concession-noni.detail: Connects two ideas when the second one is surprising or disappointing given the first.

examples.japanese: 勉強したのに、忘れました。
examples.english: Even though I studied, I forgot.
examples.note: のに often carries disappointment.

nominalizer-koto.detail: Turns an action or idea into a noun-like concept that particles can attach to.

examples.japanese: 泳ぐことが好きです。
examples.english: I like swimming.
examples.note: こと nominalizes actions or ideas.

plain-past-ta.short: plain completed action or past state
plain-past-ta.detail: Marks a plain past-tense action or state. Common verb endings include した, った, いた, いだ, and んだ.

examples.japanese: 昨日、映画を見た。
examples.english: I watched a movie yesterday.
examples.note: This is a broad detector for past forms.

sequence-te-kara.detail: Says one action happens after another action is completed.

examples.japanese: 手を洗ってから食べます。
examples.english: I eat after washing my hands.
examples.note: てから emphasizes the first action is completed first.

time-mae-ni.detail: Marks an action or event that happens before another.

examples.japanese: 寝る前に歯を磨きます。
examples.english: I brush my teeth before sleeping.
examples.note: Dictionary form + 前に means before doing.

time-ato-de-ni.detail: Marks an action or event that happens after another.

examples.japanese: 仕事の後で会いましょう。
examples.english: Let us meet after work.
examples.note: 後で is common for after.

time-toki.detail: Marks the time or occasion when something happens.

examples.japanese: 困ったとき、友だちに相談します。
examples.english: When I am in trouble, I consult a friend.
examples.note: とき marks the time of a situation.

limit-made-made-ni.detail: まで marks an endpoint; までに marks a deadline.

examples.japanese: 五時までに帰ります。
examples.english: I will return by five.
examples.note: までに means by a deadline.

comparison-yori-nohou.detail: Compares two things; より marks the thing being compared against, while の方が marks the preferred or greater side.

examples.japanese: 犬より猫の方が好きです。
examples.english: I like cats more than dogs.
examples.note: Comparison often uses both より and 方が.

superlative-ichiban.detail: Marks the highest degree among a group.

examples.japanese: 寿司が一番好きです。
examples.english: I like sushi the most.
examples.note: 一番 marks the top choice or degree.

question-ka-douka.detail: Embeds a yes-or-no question inside a larger sentence.

examples.japanese: 行くかどうかまだ決めていません。
examples.english: I have not decided whether I will go.
examples.note: かどうか embeds uncertainty.

purpose-masu-stem-ni-iku.detail: Uses a verb stem plus に行く, に来る, or に帰る to show the purpose of movement.

examples.japanese: 映画を見に行きます。
examples.english: I will go to see a movie.
examples.note: The stem before に marks what someone goes to do.

nominalizer-no.detail: Turns a verb or adjective phrase into a noun-like idea before a particle.

examples.japanese: 泳ぐのは楽しいです。
examples.english: Swimming is fun.
examples.note: の nominalizes the action before は.

quotation-to-iu.detail: Marks a name, definition, quote, or explanation.

examples.japanese: 田中さんという人に会いました。
examples.english: I met a person called Tanaka.
examples.note: という connects quoted, named, or defined content.

casual-tte.detail: Casual marker for quoting, naming, or setting a topic.

examples.japanese: 明日来るって聞きました。
examples.english: I heard that he is coming tomorrow.
examples.note: って is casual and broad.

explanation-n-desu.detail: Adds an explanatory or context-seeking tone.

examples.japanese: 頭が痛いんです。
examples.english: The thing is, my head hurts.
examples.note: んです often explains or asks for explanation.

explanation-no-da.detail: Adds explanatory force in plain speech, similar to んです in polite speech.

examples.japanese: 今日は行けないんだ。
examples.english: The thing is, I cannot go today.
examples.note: んだ gives the statement explanatory context.

existence-ga-aru-iru.detail: Uses ある for inanimate existence and いる for animate existence.

examples.japanese: 机の上に本があります。
examples.english: There is a book on the desk.
examples.note: がある marks existence or possession.

skill-ga-suki-jouzu-heta.short: like, good at, or poor at
skill-ga-suki-jouzu-heta.detail: Uses が to mark the thing liked or the skill being evaluated.

examples.japanese: 妹は料理が上手です。
examples.english: My younger sister is good at cooking.
examples.note: The evaluated skill or liked thing is marked with が.

skill-no-ga-suki.short: like or be good at doing
skill-no-ga-suki.detail: Uses の to nominalize an action before saying someone likes, dislikes, or is skilled at it.

examples.japanese: 走るのが好きです。
examples.english: I like running.
examples.note: の turns the action into the thing being evaluated.

invitation-mashou.detail: A polite way to suggest doing something together, or to offer help with ましょうか.

examples.japanese: 一緒に帰りましょう。
examples.english: Let's go home together.
examples.note: ます-stem + ましょう makes a polite invitation.

invitation-masen-ka.detail: Uses a polite negative question to invite someone or make a gentle suggestion.

examples.japanese: コーヒーを飲みませんか。
examples.english: Would you like to drink coffee?
examples.note: ませんか is a common polite invitation.

relief-te-yokatta.detail: Expresses relief or happiness that an action or situation happened.

examples.japanese: 会えてよかったです。
examples.english: I'm glad I could see you.
examples.note: てよかった means it was good that the action happened.

without-zuni.detail: Connects another action done without doing the first action.

examples.japanese: 朝ご飯を食べずに出た。
examples.english: I left without eating breakfast.
examples.note: ずに is a formal/literary negative connector.

without-naide.detail: Connects another action done without doing the first action.

examples.japanese: 傘を持たないで出かけた。
examples.english: I went out without taking an umbrella.
examples.note: ないで can mean without doing.

apology-te-sumimasen.detail: Apologizes for the action or state before てすみません.

examples.japanese: 遅れてすみません。
examples.english: I'm sorry for being late.
examples.note: てすみません gives the reason for the apology.

necessity-ga-hitsuyou.detail: Marks something as needed or necessary.

examples.japanese: 予約が必要です。
examples.english: A reservation is necessary.
examples.note: が marks the thing that is needed.

sensation-ga-suru.detail: Uses する with sensory nouns such as sound, smell, taste, or feeling.

examples.japanese: いい匂いがする。
examples.english: It smells good.
examples.note: がする often marks a perceived sensation.

case-baai.detail: Frames the condition or situation in which the next statement applies.

examples.japanese: 雨の場合は中止です。
examples.english: In case of rain, it will be cancelled.
examples.note: 場合 means case or situation.

examples-nado.short: such as or and so on
examples-nado.detail: Marks an example or non-exhaustive set.

examples.japanese: 本などを読みます。
examples.english: I read books and things like that.
examples.note: など softens or leaves the list open.

examples-toka.detail: Casually lists examples without making a complete list.

examples.japanese: 週末は映画とか見ます。
examples.english: On weekends I watch things like movies.
examples.note: とか is a casual example marker.

hearsay-to-iwarete-iru.detail: Reports what people generally say or said about something.

examples.japanese: 彼は天才と言われている。
examples.english: He is said to be a genius.
examples.note: と言われている reports a common statement.

examples.japanese: 明日は雨だと聞きました。
examples.english: I heard that it will rain tomorrow.
examples.note: と聞いた marks the heard content.

similarity-you-da.detail: Expresses resemblance, appearance, or a manner like something.

examples.japanese: 彼は疲れているようだ。
examples.english: He seems tired.
examples.note: ようだ can mean seems like or resembles.

examples.japanese: 少し考えさせてください。
examples.english: Please let me think for a bit.
examples.note: Causative て-form + ください asks to be allowed.

decision-koto-ni-suru.detail: Shows that someone decides on an action or policy.

examples.japanese: 毎朝走ることにしました。
examples.english: I decided to run every morning.
examples.note: ことにする marks personal decision.

arrangement-koto-ni-naru.detail: Shows an arrangement or outcome decided by circumstances or others.

examples.japanese: 来月転勤することになりました。
examples.english: It has been decided that I will transfer next month.
examples.note: Often implies an external decision.

honorific-o-go-ni-naru-suru.detail: Uses お or ご with a verb noun or stem for respectful or humble speech.

examples.japanese: 社長がお帰りになります。
examples.english: The president will return.
examples.note: Regex can flag the construction, but politeness role depends on the verb.

polite-gozaimasu.detail: A very polite form related to ある or です in set expressions.

examples.japanese: 質問がございます。
examples.english: I have a question.
examples.note: ございます is very polite.

advice-beki.detail: Expresses what is proper, expected, or advisable.

examples.japanese: 約束は守るべきです。
examples.english: You should keep promises.
examples.note: べき is stronger and more formal than 方がいい.

time-aida-aida-ni.detail: Marks a period during which something happens.

examples.japanese: 夏休みの間に本を三冊読みました。
examples.english: I read three books during summer vacation.
examples.note: 間に focuses on something happening within the interval.

time-uchi-ni.short: while still or before it changes
time-uchi-ni.detail: Says to act while a condition still holds.

examples.japanese: 明るいうちに帰りましょう。
examples.english: Let us go home while it is still light.
examples.note: うちに warns the condition may change.

time-saichuu-ni.detail: Marks that something happens right in the middle of another action.

examples.japanese: 会議の最中に電話が鳴った。
examples.english: The phone rang in the middle of the meeting.
examples.note: 最中に emphasizes interruption during an event.

repetition-tabi-ni.detail: Marks something that happens each time another thing occurs.

examples.japanese: 彼に会うたびに元気をもらう。
examples.english: Every time I meet him, I feel encouraged.
examples.note: たびに repeats with each occurrence.

incidental-tsuide-ni.detail: Adds an extra action done along with the main action.

examples.japanese: 買い物のついでに郵便局へ行きます。
examples.english: I will go to the post office while I am out shopping.
examples.note: ついでに adds a convenient side task.

phase-compound-verb.short: begin, start, continue, or finish doing
phase-compound-verb.detail: Adds a phase such as beginning, starting suddenly, continuing, or finishing to a verb stem.

examples.japanese: 雨が降り始めました。
examples.english: It started raining.
examples.note: Verb stem + 始める marks the start of an action.

state-ppanashi.detail: Says something remains in a state, often because it was left that way.

examples.japanese: 電気をつけっぱなしにした。
examples.english: I left the light on.
examples.note: っぱなし often has a negative nuance.

covered-darake.detail: Says something is full of an undesirable thing.

examples.japanese: 服が泥だらけだ。
examples.english: My clothes are covered in mud.
examples.note: だらけ often marks an unpleasant abundance.

fresh-tate.detail: Describes something that has just been made or done.

examples.japanese: 焼きたてのパンを買った。
examples.english: I bought freshly baked bread.
examples.note: たて attaches to a verb stem.

elapsed-buri-ni.detail: Marks that something happens after a stated interval.

examples.japanese: 三年ぶりに友だちに会った。
examples.english: I met my friend for the first time in three years.
examples.note: ぶりに measures time since the previous occurrence.

interval-goto-ni.detail: Marks a repeated interval or every member of a set.

examples.japanese: 会うごとに日本語が上手になる。
examples.english: Every time we meet, your Japanese gets better.
examples.note: ごとに means each or every.

examples.japanese: 一日おきに運動します。
examples.english: I exercise every other day.
examples.note: おきに marks spacing between occurrences.

emphasis-kara-koso.detail: Emphasizes the reason before からこそ as the key cause.

examples.japanese: 大切だからこそ厳しく言う。
examples.english: I say it strictly precisely because it is important.
examples.note: からこそ strengthens the reason.

source-ni-yoru-to.detail: Marks the source of information or a report.

examples.japanese: ニュースによると雪です。
examples.english: According to the news, it will snow.
examples.note: によると introduces the information source.

topic-ni-kansuru.detail: Modifies a noun by saying what it is about or related to.

examples.japanese: 環境に関する問題を話し合う。
examples.english: We discuss problems related to the environment.
examples.note: に関する is the noun-modifying form of に関して.

context-ni-okeru.detail: Formal noun-modifying marker for field, time, place, or context.

examples.japanese: 現代における課題です。
examples.english: It is an issue in the present day.
examples.note: における modifies a following noun.

standard-ni-shite-wa.detail: Judges something as unexpected compared with the marked standard.

examples.japanese: 子どもにしては上手です。
examples.english: For a child, they are skilled.
examples.note: にしては compares against expectations.

simultaneous-to-douji-ni.detail: Marks two things happening at the same time, or two simultaneous qualities.

examples.japanese: 卒業と同時に働き始めた。
examples.english: I started working at the same time as graduation.
examples.note: と同時に links simultaneous events.

supposition-to-shitara.detail: Sets up a hypothetical assumption before giving a result or judgment.

examples.japanese: 行くとしたら明日です。
examples.english: If I were to go, it would be tomorrow.
examples.note: としたら sets a supposition.

almost-tokoro-datta.detail: Says something nearly happened, often something undesirable.

examples.japanese: 電車に遅れるところだった。
examples.english: I almost missed the train.
examples.note: ところだった marks a near event.

nonlimiting-wa-mochiron.detail: Marks something as obvious and adds more beyond it.

examples.japanese: 日本語はもちろん英語も必要です。
examples.english: English is necessary, not only Japanese.
examples.note: はもちろん often pairs with も.

pretend-furi-wo-suru.detail: Describes pretending or acting as if something is true.

examples.japanese: 知らないふりをした。
examples.english: I pretended not to know.
examples.note: ふりをする means to pretend.

instant-ta-totan-ni.detail: Says something happened immediately after another action.

examples.japanese: 外に出たとたん雨が降った。
examples.english: The moment I went outside, it started raining.
examples.note: たとたんに marks an immediate result.

difficulty-gatai.detail: Says an action is difficult to do, often psychologically or emotionally.

examples.japanese: 信じがたい話です。
examples.english: It is a hard-to-believe story.
examples.note: がたい attaches to a verb stem.

only-shika-nai.detail: Says there is no option other than doing or choosing the marked thing.

examples.japanese: やるしかない。
examples.english: There is nothing to do but do it.
examples.note: しかない creates a strong only-choice meaning.

emphasis-sae.detail: Emphasizes an extreme or surprising example.

examples.japanese: 子どもでさえ知っています。
examples.english: Even children know it.
examples.note: さえ highlights an unexpected minimum or extreme.

emphasis-koso.detail: Strongly emphasizes the marked word as the important one.

examples.japanese: 今こそ始めよう。
examples.english: Now is exactly the time to begin.
examples.note: こそ gives focused emphasis.

try-te-goran.detail: A casual or gentle instruction to try doing something.

examples.japanese: 食べてごらん。
examples.english: Try eating it.
examples.note: てごらん is often used by adults toward children or close listeners.

cause-sei-okage-de.detail: せいで gives a negative cause; おかげで gives a beneficial cause.

examples.japanese: 先生のおかげで合格できました。
examples.english: Thanks to my teacher, I was able to pass.
examples.note: おかげで is positive; せいで is negative.

manner-toori.detail: Says something happens in the same way as a model or statement.

examples.japanese: 説明のとおりに操作してください。
examples.english: Please operate it as explained.
examples.note: とおり means following a model.

certainty-ni-chigai-nai.detail: Shows strong certainty based on evidence or reasoning.

examples.japanese: 彼は医者に違いない。
examples.english: He must be a doctor.
examples.note: に違いない is strong certainty.

examples.japanese: 彼なら勝つに決まっている。
examples.english: If it is him, he is sure to win.
examples.note: Often sounds emphatic or subjective.

qualification-to-wa-kagiranai.detail: Says something is not always or not necessarily true.

examples.japanese: 高いものが良いとは限りません。
examples.english: Expensive things are not necessarily good.
examples.note: とは限らない denies universality.

contrast-ippou-de.short: on the other hand or while
contrast-ippou-de.detail: Marks contrast, parallel facts, or one aspect of a situation.

examples.japanese: 収入が増えた一方で、忙しくなった。
examples.english: My income increased, but on the other hand I became busier.
examples.note: 一方で compares two sides.

contrast-hanmen.detail: Contrasts one side of something with another side.

examples.japanese: 便利な反面、危険もある。
examples.english: It is convenient, but on the other hand there are dangers.
examples.note: 反面 marks the opposite side.

substitution-kawari-ni.short: instead of or in exchange for
substitution-kawari-ni.detail: Marks a substitute action or a tradeoff.

examples.japanese: 映画に行くかわりに家で休みます。
examples.english: Instead of going to a movie, I will rest at home.
examples.note: かわりに marks replacement or exchange.

topic-ni-kanshite.detail: Marks the topic of discussion or concern.

examples.japanese: 仕事に関して相談があります。
examples.english: I have something to discuss about work.
examples.note: に関して is formal topic marking.

examples.japanese: 去年に比べて暑いです。
examples.english: It is hot compared with last year.
examples.note: に比べて sets comparison baseline.

basis-ni-motozuite.detail: Marks the basis or evidence for an action or judgment.

examples.japanese: データに基づいて判断します。
examples.english: We will decide based on data.
examples.note: に基づいて is formal.

following-ni-sotte.short: along with or in line with
following-ni-sotte.detail: Shows that something follows a rule, plan, or path.

examples.japanese: 計画に沿って進めます。
examples.english: We will proceed according to the plan.
examples.note: に沿って follows a route or plan.

following-change-ni-shitagatte.detail: Marks following a rule, person, or gradual change.

examples.japanese: 説明に従って操作してください。
examples.english: Please operate it according to the instructions.
examples.note: Can also mean as something changes.

change-ni-tsurete.detail: Shows one change happening together with another.

examples.japanese: 寒くなるにつれて人が減った。
examples.english: As it got colder, fewer people came.
examples.note: につれて links gradual changes.

together-to-tomo-ni.detail: Marks doing something together or a change occurring alongside another.

examples.japanese: 時代とともに言葉も変わる。
examples.english: Language changes along with the times.
examples.note: Formal together/change marker.

context-ni-oite.detail: Formal marker for place, field, time, or context.

examples.japanese: 現代社会において重要です。
examples.english: It is important in modern society.
examples.note: において is formal and written.

means-wo-tsuujite-tooshite.detail: Marks a means, mediator, or time span.

examples.japanese: 一年を通して暖かいです。
examples.english: It is warm throughout the year.
examples.note: を通じて/通して can mean through or throughout.

representative-wo-hajime.detail: Introduces a leading example from a larger group.

examples.japanese: 東京をはじめ多くの都市で行われた。
examples.english: It was held in many cities, starting with Tokyo.
examples.note: をはじめ introduces a representative item.

limit-ni-kagiru-kagirazu.short: limited to, not limited to, or best
limit-ni-kagiru-kagirazu.detail: Marks limitation, non-limitation, special cases, or a strong recommendation.

examples.japanese: 疲れた時は寝るに限る。
examples.english: When tired, sleeping is best.
examples.note: に限る can also recommend the best option.

suffix-gachi.detail: Shows a repeated tendency, often negative.

examples.japanese: 忙しいと食事を忘れがちです。
examples.english: When busy, I tend to forget meals.
examples.note: がち often marks an undesirable tendency.

suffix-gimi.detail: Shows that something is a little in a certain state.

examples.japanese: 今日は疲れ気味です。
examples.english: I am a bit tired today.
examples.note: 気味 is a slight tendency or condition.

suffix-ge.detail: Adds a sense that someone or something appears a certain way.

examples.japanese: 彼は寂しげに笑った。
examples.english: He smiled sadly.
examples.note: げ often describes visible mood.

suffix-ppoi.detail: Shows something seems like, is prone to, or has a quality.

examples.japanese: この服は子どもっぽい。
examples.english: These clothes look childish.
examples.note: っぽい is casual and broad.

negative-youni-nai.detail: Says there is no method or possibility for doing something.

examples.japanese: 壊れすぎて直しようがない。
examples.english: It is too broken to fix.
examples.note: Stem + ようがない means no way to do.

impossible-kkonai.detail: Casually says something will not or cannot happen.

examples.japanese: 彼が負けっこない。
examples.english: There is no way he will lose.
examples.note: っこない is casual and emphatic.

condition-kara-ni-wa.detail: Sets a condition that creates obligation, resolve, or expectation.

examples.japanese: やるからには最後までやります。
examples.english: Since I am doing it, I will do it to the end.
examples.note: からには often implies commitment.

qualification-kara-to-itte.detail: Introduces a reason that is not enough to justify the following conclusion.

examples.japanese: 安いからといって、買うとは限らない。
examples.english: Just because it is cheap does not mean I will buy it.
examples.note: Often pairs with a negative or limiting conclusion.

condition-nai-kagiri.detail: Says the following result holds unless the negative condition changes.

examples.japanese: 雨が降らない限り、試合は行われます。
examples.english: Unless it rains, the match will be held.
examples.note: ない限り means unless.

condition-ijou-wa.detail: Sets a condition that creates obligation or consequence.

examples.japanese: 約束した以上は守るべきだ。
examples.english: Since you promised, you should keep it.
examples.note: 以上は is formal and firm.

condition-ue-wa.detail: Means now that something is true, a certain responsibility follows.

examples.japanese: 引き受けた上は全力を尽くします。
examples.english: Now that I have accepted, I will do my best.
examples.note: 上は is formal.

sequence-ue-de.short: after doing or on the basis of
sequence-ue-de.detail: Means after doing something, or after considering something as a basis.

examples.japanese: 内容を確認した上で署名します。
examples.english: I will sign after confirming the contents.
examples.note: 上で often means after careful action.

addition-ue-ni.detail: Adds another fact, often intensifying the evaluation.

examples.japanese: 彼は親切な上に面白い。
examples.english: He is kind and, on top of that, funny.
examples.note: 上に stacks positive or negative facts.

viewpoint-kara-miru-to.short: from the point of view of
viewpoint-kara-miru-to.detail: Marks the standpoint or basis for judgment.

examples.japanese: 専門家から見ると簡単です。
examples.english: From an expert's view, it is simple.
examples.note: から見ると introduces a viewpoint.

starting-kara-shite.detail: Marks a representative starting point for judgment.

examples.japanese: 名前からして怪しい。
examples.english: Even the name sounds suspicious.
examples.note: からして can mean judging from or even.

concession-ni-shitemo-toshitemo.detail: Sets up an assumed case and says the next point still applies.

examples.japanese: 行くにしても、早めに連絡してください。
examples.english: Even if you go, please contact me early.
examples.note: にしても and としても introduce a conceded case.

concession-ni-shiro-ni-seyo.detail: Marks a conceded case or one side of an alternative pair.

examples.japanese: 賛成にせよ反対にせよ、理由を説明してください。
examples.english: Whether you agree or disagree, please explain why.
examples.note: Often repeats for A or B alternatives.

after-all-ageku.detail: Marks a final, often disappointing result after a long process.

examples.japanese: 長く迷ったあげく、買わないことにした。
examples.english: After much hesitation, I decided not to buy it.
examples.note: あげく often carries a negative result.

after-effort-sue-ni.detail: Marks a result reached after effort, discussion, or time.

examples.japanese: 何度も話し合った末に、計画を変更した。
examples.english: After many discussions, we changed the plan.
examples.note: 末に emphasizes the process before the result.

only-ni-suginai.detail: Says something is only a certain thing and should not be overestimated.

examples.japanese: これは一例にすぎません。
examples.english: This is nothing more than one example.
examples.note: にすぎない minimizes.

essence-ni-hoka-naranai.detail: States the true identity or central cause of something.

examples.japanese: 成功は努力の結果にほかならない。
examples.english: Success is nothing other than the result of effort.
examples.note: Formal emphatic conclusion.

necessity-zaru-wo-enai.detail: Says there is no choice but to do something.

examples.japanese: 予定を変更せざるを得ない。
examples.english: We have no choice but to change the plan.
examples.note: ざるを得ない is formal necessity.

compulsion-zu-ni-wa-irarenai.detail: Says one cannot resist doing or feeling something.

examples.japanese: 笑わずにはいられなかった。
examples.english: I could not help laughing.
examples.note: Often used for emotions or impulses.

possibility-eru-enai.detail: Marks something as possible or impossible, often in formal writing.

examples.japanese: 事故は起こり得る。
examples.english: An accident can happen.
examples.note: 得る is read うる or える depending on form.

risk-kanenai.detail: Warns that a negative result could happen.

examples.japanese: このままでは失敗しかねない。
examples.english: At this rate, we might fail.
examples.note: かねない is used for undesirable possibilities.

difficulty-kaneru.detail: Politely says something is difficult or impossible to do.

examples.japanese: その質問には答えかねます。
examples.english: I am unable to answer that question.
examples.note: Often used in formal refusal.

emotion-te-naranai.detail: Expresses a strong spontaneous feeling or state.

examples.japanese: 心配でならない。
examples.english: I cannot help being worried.
examples.note: Used with feelings and sensations.

emotion-te-tamaranai.detail: Expresses an intense feeling or sensation.

examples.japanese: 眠くてたまらない。
examples.english: I am unbearably sleepy.
examples.note: てたまらない intensifies feeling.

emotion-te-shouganai.detail: Expresses an uncontrollable or very strong feeling.

examples.japanese: 楽しみでしょうがない。
examples.english: I am extremely excited.
examples.note: Casual form of intense feeling.

timing-shidai.short: as soon as or depending on
timing-shidai.detail: Can mean as soon as something happens, or depending on something.

examples.japanese: 準備ができ次第、出発します。
examples.english: We will leave as soon as preparations are ready.
examples.note: 次第 is context-dependent.

time-sai-ni.detail: Formal marker for when doing something or when something happens.

examples.japanese: 申し込む際に必要です。
examples.english: It is needed when applying.
examples.note: 際に is formal when/occasion.

occasion-ni-atatte.detail: Formal marker for a special occasion, often with preparation.

examples.japanese: 開始にあたって説明します。
examples.english: I will explain before we begin.
examples.note: にあたって often marks an important occasion.

occasion-ni-saishite.detail: Formal marker for a special time or event.

examples.japanese: 卒業に際して一言述べます。
examples.english: I will say a few words on the occasion of graduation.
examples.note: に際して is formal.

prior-ni-sakidatte.detail: Marks something done before an event.

examples.japanese: 会議に先立って資料を配った。
examples.english: Materials were distributed before the meeting.
examples.note: Formal prior-to marker.

trigger-wo-kikkake-ni.detail: Marks an event that becomes the trigger for change.

examples.japanese: 留学をきっかけに日本語を始めた。
examples.english: Studying abroad triggered me to start Japanese.
examples.note: きっかけ is a trigger or opportunity.

trigger-wo-keiki-ni.detail: Formal version of using something as a turning point or trigger.

examples.japanese: 受賞を契機に仕事が増えた。
examples.english: After the award, work increased.
examples.note: 契機 is formal turning point.

span-ni-watatte.detail: Marks a span of time, place, or range.

examples.japanese: 会議は三日間にわたって行われた。
examples.english: The conference was held over three days.
examples.note: にわたって emphasizes breadth or duration.

examples.japanese: 人口の増加に伴って問題も増えた。
examples.english: Problems increased along with the population.
examples.note: に伴って is formal.

response-ni-oujite.detail: Shows something changes in response to a condition.

examples.japanese: 年齢に応じて料金が変わります。
examples.english: The fee changes according to age.
examples.note: に応じて means responding to a condition.

basis-wo-fumaete.detail: Marks information used as a basis for judgment or action.

examples.japanese: 結果を踏まえて改善します。
examples.english: We will improve based on the results.
examples.note: を踏まえて means taking into account.

merit-dake-atte.detail: Says a result is natural given the quality or status.

examples.japanese: 有名なだけあって、おいしい。
examples.english: As expected from its fame, it is delicious.
examples.note: だけあって praises or acknowledges a reason.

because-dake-ni.detail: Shows a result is especially true because of the reason.

examples.japanese: 大切なだけに失敗したくない。
examples.english: Because it is important, I do not want to fail.
examples.note: だけに intensifies the reason.

concession-youga-maiga.detail: Says that the result is the same regardless of which condition occurs.

examples.japanese: 雨が降ろうが降るまいが行きます。
examples.english: I will go whether it rains or not.
examples.note: Volitional-like form + が pairs with まいが.

concession-nagara-mo.detail: Connects a fact with a contrasting result.

examples.japanese: 狭いながらも快適な部屋です。
examples.english: It is a small but comfortable room.
examples.note: ながらも is concessive.

continuation-tsutsu.detail: Can mean while doing, although, or gradually developing with つつある.

examples.japanese: 状況は改善しつつある。
examples.english: The situation is gradually improving.
examples.note: つつある marks ongoing change.

cause-bakari-ni.detail: Marks a cause that led to an unfortunate result.

examples.japanese: 一言言ったばかりに誤解された。
examples.english: Just because I said one word, I was misunderstood.
examples.note: ばかりに usually has regret.

contrast-dokoro-ka.detail: Rejects one idea and gives a stronger or opposite fact.

examples.japanese: 暇どころか、忙しすぎます。
examples.english: Far from being free, I am too busy.
examples.note: どころか heightens contrast.

impossible-dokoro-dewa-nai.detail: Says the situation makes something impossible or inappropriate.

examples.japanese: 遊ぶどころではない。
examples.english: This is no time to play.
examples.note: どころではない rejects possibility due to circumstances.

nonlimiting-dake-denaku.detail: Adds another thing beyond the first.

examples.japanese: 彼は日本語だけでなく韓国語も話せる。
examples.english: He can speak not only Japanese but also Korean.
examples.note: Often pairs with も.

regardless-ni-kakawarazu.detail: Says the result is the same regardless of a condition.

examples.japanese: 年齢にかかわらず参加できます。
examples.english: You can participate regardless of age.
examples.note: Do not confuse with にもかかわらず (despite).

contrary-ni-hanshite.detail: Marks a result contrary to expectation, rule, or intention.

examples.japanese: 予想に反して売れた。
examples.english: It sold contrary to expectations.
examples.note: に反して means against or contrary to.

examples.japanese: 家賃に加えて光熱費も必要です。
examples.english: Utilities are needed in addition to rent.
examples.note: に加えて is formal addition.

target-ni-kotaete.detail: Acts in response to expectations, requests, or support.

examples.japanese: 期待に応えて頑張ります。
examples.english: I will work hard in response to expectations.
examples.note: に応えて responds to people or expectations.

center-wo-chuushin-ni.detail: Marks the central person, place, or topic.

examples.japanese: 東京を中心に活動しています。
examples.english: We operate mainly around Tokyo.
examples.note: を中心に marks the center.

regardless-wo-toyazu.detail: Says a distinction does not matter.

examples.japanese: 経験を問わず応募できます。
examples.english: You can apply regardless of experience.
examples.note: を問わず is formal.

topic-wo-megutte.detail: Marks an issue around which discussion, conflict, or movement occurs.

examples.japanese: 予算をめぐって議論が続いた。
examples.english: Debate continued over the budget.
examples.note: Often used with disputes or discussion.

direction-muke-muki.detail: 向け means aimed at; 向き means suitable for.

examples.japanese: これは初心者向けの本です。
examples.english: This is a book for beginners.
examples.note: 向け targets; 向き suits.

relative-wari-ni.detail: Shows something is unexpected relative to a standard.

examples.japanese: 値段のわりにおいしい。
examples.english: It is tasty considering the price.
examples.note: わりに compares against expectation.

memory-kke.detail: Casually checks memory or confirms something.

examples.japanese: 明日の会議は何時だっけ。
examples.english: What time was tomorrow's meeting again?
examples.note: っけ is casual recollection.

quote-to-iu-yori.detail: Corrects or reframes the previous description.

examples.japanese: 彼は静かというより無口だ。
examples.english: He is not so much quiet as taciturn.
examples.note: というより adjusts the label.

examples.japanese: 京都や奈良といった古い町。
examples.english: Old cities such as Kyoto and Nara.
examples.note: といった lists examples.

topic-to-ieba.detail: Introduces something associated with a topic.

examples.japanese: 日本の食べ物といえば寿司です。
examples.english: Speaking of Japanese food, sushi comes to mind.
examples.note: といえば sets up an association.

thing-mono-da.detail: Can express general truths, emotional reflection, or past habits.

examples.japanese: 時間が経つのは早いものです。
examples.english: Time really does pass quickly.
examples.note: ものだ is context-sensitive.

cause-mono-dakara.detail: Gives a reason, often as an excuse or explanation.

examples.japanese: 道が混んでいたものだから遅れました。
examples.english: I was late because the road was crowded.
examples.note: ものだから softens an explanation.

concession-mono-no.detail: States a fact but contrasts it with an unexpected result.

examples.japanese: 買ったものの、まだ使っていない。
examples.english: Although I bought it, I have not used it yet.
examples.note: ものの is written-style concession.

advice-koto-da.detail: Gives advice or states what is important.

examples.japanese: 上達したいなら練習することだ。
examples.english: If you want to improve, you should practice.
examples.note: ことだ can be advice.

unnecessary-koto-wa-nai.detail: Says there is no need to do something.

examples.japanese: そんなに心配することはない。
examples.english: There is no need to worry so much.
examples.note: ことはない removes necessity.

double-negative-nai-koto-wa-nai.detail: Double negative that gives a qualified yes.

examples.japanese: できないことはない。
examples.english: It is not that I cannot do it.
examples.note: Often means possible, but not easily or enthusiastically.

explanation-to-iu-koto-da.detail: Explains a conclusion or reports information.

examples.japanese: つまり中止ということです。
examples.english: In other words, it means it is cancelled.
examples.note: Can be explanation or hearsay.

nature-to-iu-mono-da.detail: States a general evaluation or conclusion.

examples.japanese: それが親切というものだ。
examples.english: That is what kindness is.
examples.note: Often makes a normative evaluation.

not-nature-to-iu-mono-dewa-nai.detail: Says something is not simply or always the case.

examples.japanese: 高ければ良いというものではない。
examples.english: Expensive does not necessarily mean good.
examples.note: 否定 of というものだ.

wish-nai-mono-ka.detail: Expresses a wish that something could happen.

examples.japanese: もっと簡単にできないものか。
examples.english: Is there no way to do it more easily?
examples.note: Often expresses longing for a solution.

instant-ga-hayai-ka.detail: Shows one action happens immediately after another.

examples.japanese: ドアを開けるが早いか、犬が飛び出した。
examples.english: No sooner had I opened the door than the dog jumped out.
examples.note: Literary immediate sequence.

instant-ya-inaya.detail: Shows an action happens immediately after another.

examples.japanese: ベルが鳴るや否や、生徒が立ち上がった。
examples.english: As soon as the bell rang, the students stood up.
examples.note: Formal/literary immediate sequence.

instant-nari.detail: Shows one action immediately follows another, often unexpectedly.

examples.japanese: 彼は帰るなり寝てしまった。
examples.english: As soon as he got home, he fell asleep.
examples.note: N1 なり differs from listing なり.

repetition-soba-kara.detail: Shows something happens repeatedly right after another action, often frustratingly.

examples.japanese: 覚えたそばから忘れる。
examples.english: I forget things as soon as I learn them.
examples.note: Often negative or frustrating.

unexpected-ka-to-omoi-kiya.detail: Introduces an unexpected result contrary to what one thought.

examples.japanese: 終わったかと思いきや、また問題が出た。
examples.english: Just when I thought it was over, another problem appeared.
examples.note: 思いきや signals reversal.

incidental-katagata.detail: Marks an action done also for another purpose, often formal visits or thanks.

examples.japanese: お礼かたがた伺いました。
examples.english: I visited also to express my thanks.
examples.note: Formal combined purpose.

incidental-gatera.detail: Marks doing something while also doing another activity.

examples.japanese: 散歩がてら買い物に行く。
examples.english: I will go shopping while taking a walk.
examples.note: がてら is like ついでに but more lexical.

starting-wo-kawakiri-ni.detail: Marks the first in a series.

examples.japanese: 東京を皮切りに全国で上映される。
examples.english: Starting with Tokyo, it will be shown nationwide.
examples.note: 皮切り is the opening event.

endpoint-wo-kagiri-ni.detail: Marks a final point or last occurrence.

examples.japanese: 今日を限りに退職します。
examples.english: As of today, I will resign.
examples.note: を限りに marks an endpoint.

means-wo-motte.detail: Formal marker for means, reason, or endpoint.

examples.japanese: 本日をもって終了します。
examples.english: This ends as of today.
examples.note: をもって is formal.

turning-wo-sakai-ni.detail: Marks a boundary after which things change.

examples.japanese: 結婚を境に生活が変わった。
examples.english: My life changed after marriage.
examples.note: 境 marks a boundary.

range-ni-itaru-made.detail: Emphasizes a range reaching even to a point.

examples.japanese: 細部に至るまで確認した。
examples.english: I checked everything down to the details.
examples.note: に至るまで emphasizes breadth.

stage-ni-itatte.short: only when / at the stage of
stage-ni-itatte.detail: Marks reaching a serious or notable stage.

examples.japanese: 事態がここに至っては手遅れだ。
examples.english: At this stage, it is too late.
examples.note: に至っては emphasizes a reached state.

context-ni-atte.detail: Formal marker for being in a special situation or position.

examples.japanese: 困難な状況にあって冷静だった。
examples.english: He was calm in a difficult situation.
examples.note: Formal written expression.

standard-ni-sokushite.detail: Shows action follows facts, rules, or reality closely.

examples.japanese: 現実に即して考える。
examples.english: Think in line with reality.
examples.note: に即して is formal.

exclusive-wo-oite.detail: Says there is no better or other option than the marked item.

examples.japanese: 彼をおいて適任者はいない。
examples.english: There is no one more suitable than him.
examples.note: Often used with いない or ない.

defiance-wo-mono-to-mo-sezu.detail: Says someone acts without being daunted by difficulty.

examples.japanese: 悪天候をものともせず進んだ。
examples.english: They advanced despite the bad weather.
examples.note: Heroic or formal tone.

forced-wo-yogi-naku-sareru.detail: Says someone is forced by circumstances into a result.

examples.japanese: 計画の変更を余儀なくされた。
examples.english: We were forced to change the plan.
examples.note: Noun + を余儀なくされる.

force-wo-yogi-naku-saseru.detail: Says circumstances force someone into a result.

examples.japanese: 大雪が中止を余儀なくさせた。
examples.english: Heavy snow forced the cancellation.
examples.note: Cause version of 余儀なくされる.

emotion-ni-taenai.detail: Can express unbearable negativity or deep positive emotion depending on noun.

examples.japanese: 感謝に堪えません。
examples.english: I cannot thank you enough.
examples.note: Often formal with 感謝 or 遺憾.

reluctance-ni-shinobinai.detail: Says one cannot bring oneself to do something emotionally.

examples.japanese: 彼に真実を言うに忍びない。
examples.english: I cannot bear to tell him the truth.
examples.note: Emotional reluctance.

easy-inference-ni-katagunai.detail: Says something is easy to imagine or understand.

examples.japanese: 彼の苦労は想像に難くない。
examples.english: His hardship is not hard to imagine.
examples.note: Usually with 想像 or 理解.

worthy-ni-ataru.detail: Marks something as deserving an evaluation or action.

examples.japanese: この本は読むに値する。
examples.english: This book is worth reading.
examples.note: に値する means worth doing/evaluating.

sufficient-ni-taru.detail: Shows something is sufficient or worthy for a judgment.

examples.japanese: 信頼に足る人物です。
examples.english: He is a person worthy of trust.
examples.note: Formal sufficiency/worth.

utmost-no-itari.detail: Expresses an extreme degree, often in set phrases.

examples.japanese: 光栄の至りです。
examples.english: It is the height of honor.
examples.note: Formal set expression.

extreme-kiwamaru-kiwamarinai.detail: Expresses an extreme degree, often negative or formal.

examples.japanese: 失礼極まりない態度だ。
examples.english: That is an extremely rude attitude.
examples.note: N1 formal intensifier.

deep-wish-te-yamanai.detail: Expresses a deep, continuing wish or feeling.

examples.japanese: 成功を願ってやみません。
examples.english: I sincerely wish for your success.
examples.note: Formal with wishes and feelings.

since-te-kara-to-iu-mono.detail: Says that after an event, a state has continued.

examples.japanese: 犬を飼ってからというもの、毎日が楽しい。
examples.english: Ever since getting a dog, every day has been fun.
examples.note: Emphasizes lasting change.

consequence-zu-ni-wa-okanai.detail: Says something will inevitably cause an action or reaction.

examples.japanese: この映画は人を感動させずにはおかない。
examples.english: This movie is sure to move people.
examples.note: Often means cannot fail to affect.

consequence-zu-ni-wa-sumanai.detail: Says one cannot get away without doing something.

examples.japanese: 謝らずにはすまない。
examples.english: I cannot avoid apologizing.
examples.note: Duty or consequence cannot be avoided.

prohibition-bekarazu.detail: Old/formal prohibition often seen on signs or set phrases.

examples.japanese: ここに入るべからず。
examples.english: Do not enter here.
examples.note: Literary/formal prohibition.

improper-majiki.detail: Marks behavior as inappropriate for a role or status.

examples.japanese: 教師にあるまじき行為だ。
examples.english: That is behavior unbecoming of a teacher.
examples.note: Formal judgment of impropriety.

role-taru-mono.detail: States what is expected of someone in a role.

examples.japanese: リーダーたるもの責任を持つべきだ。
examples.english: A leader should take responsibility.
examples.note: Formal role-based expectation.

surprise-tomo-arou-mono-ga.detail: Expresses criticism or surprise that someone of a status did something.

examples.japanese: 医者ともあろうものが不注意だった。
examples.english: A doctor, of all people, was careless.
examples.note: Critical surprise.

stage-tomo-naru-to.detail: Says that once something reaches a level, things change.

examples.japanese: 大人ともなると責任が増える。
examples.english: Once you become an adult, responsibilities increase.
examples.note: Marks a stage or status.

any-de-are.detail: Formal marker meaning even if or no matter what.

examples.japanese: 理由が何であれ、許されない。
examples.english: Whatever the reason, it is not allowed.
examples.note: Often pairs with repeated alternatives.

pair-to-ii-to-ii.detail: Picks two examples to evaluate the whole.

examples.japanese: デザインといい性能といい素晴らしい。
examples.english: Both the design and performance are excellent.
examples.note: Usually repeats といい.

concession-to-wa-ie.short: although / be that as it may
concession-to-wa-ie.detail: Acknowledges a fact but introduces a contrasting point.

examples.japanese: 春とはいえ、まだ寒い。
examples.english: Although it is spring, it is still cold.
examples.note: Formal concession.

without-nakushite.detail: Says something cannot happen without the marked thing.

examples.japanese: 努力なくして成功はない。
examples.english: There is no success without effort.
examples.note: Formal without-condition.

basis-atte-no.detail: Says something exists thanks to another thing.

examples.japanese: 皆さんの協力あっての成功です。
examples.english: This success is thanks to everyone's cooperation.
examples.note: AあってのB = B exists because of A.

unique-nara-dewa.detail: Marks something as unique to the source.

examples.japanese: 京都ならではの雰囲気。
examples.english: An atmosphere unique to Kyoto.
examples.note: Often positive uniqueness.

covered-mamire.detail: Says something is covered in an unpleasant substance.

examples.japanese: 泥まみれになった。
examples.english: I got covered in mud.
examples.note: Often negative physical covering.

full-zukume.detail: Says everything is of one kind, often color or events.

examples.japanese: 今日はいいことずくめだった。
examples.english: Today was full of good things.
examples.note: ずくめ means entirely filled with.

depending-ikan.detail: Formal expression for depending on how something is, or regardless of it.

examples.japanese: 結果いかんで判断します。
examples.english: We will decide depending on the result.
examples.note: いかん is formal and noun-based.

result-shimatsu-da.detail: Describes a bad final result after a sequence of events.

examples.japanese: 最後には怒り出す始末だ。
examples.english: In the end, he even got angry.
examples.note: Often negative outcome.

rhetorical-denakute-nandarou.detail: Strongly asserts that something is exactly the named thing.

examples.japanese: これが愛でなくてなんだろう。
examples.english: What could this be if not love?
examples.note: Rhetorical affirmation.

extreme-to-ittara-nai.detail: Expresses an extreme degree that is hard to describe.

examples.japanese: うれしいといったらない。
examples.english: I was indescribably happy.
examples.note: Casual/emphatic extreme degree.

examples.japanese: 面倒くさいったらありゃしない。
examples.english: It is unbelievably troublesome.
examples.note: Often colloquial.

best-ni-koshita-koto-wa-nai.detail: Says that a certain option is best if possible.

examples.japanese: 早いに越したことはない。
examples.english: The earlier, the better.
examples.note: に越したことはない recommends ideal condition.

excess-ni-mo-hodo-ga-aru.detail: Criticizes something as going too far.

examples.japanese: 冗談にもほどがある。
examples.english: There is a limit to joking.
examples.note: Used for criticism.

emphatic-no-nanno.detail: Casual emphatic expression for a strong feeling or state.

examples.japanese: 忙しいのなんの。
examples.english: I was incredibly busy.
examples.note: Colloquial intensity.

minimal-tari-tomo.detail: Emphasizes even the smallest amount, often with negatives.

examples.japanese: 一秒たりとも無駄にしない。
examples.english: I will not waste even one second.
examples.note: Strong minimal emphasis.

minimal-dani.detail: Literary marker often in set phrases like 想像だにしない.

examples.japanese: 想像だにしなかった。
examples.english: I had not even imagined it.
examples.note: Literary and limited use.

minimal-sura.detail: Emphasizes an extreme or minimal example.

examples.japanese: 彼は名前すら書けない。
examples.english: He cannot even write his name.
examples.note: すら is similar to さえ but formal/literary.

comparison-gotoki.detail: Formal/literary expression meaning like, or dismissively such as.

examples.japanese: 私ごときには無理です。
examples.english: It is impossible for someone like me.
examples.note: Often humble or dismissive.

suffix-meku.detail: Means to become like or show signs of something.

examples.japanese: 春めいてきました。
examples.english: It has started to feel like spring.
examples.note: Often seasonal or atmospheric.

unnecessary-made-mo-nai.detail: Says something is so obvious or unnecessary that it need not be done.

examples.japanese: 言うまでもない。
examples.english: It goes without saying.
examples.note: までもない removes need.

unnecessary-ni-wa-oyobanai.short: no need or not equal to
unnecessary-ni-wa-oyobanai.detail: Can mean no need to do, or not reaching the level of something.

examples.japanese: 心配するには及びません。
examples.english: There is no need to worry.
examples.note: Formal expression.

situation-tokoro-wo.detail: Politely acknowledges someone's situation, often in thanks or apology.

examples.japanese: お忙しいところをありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you despite being busy.
examples.note: Common polite set pattern.
